sections.title: Diagnosis Summary
sections.content:
**Primary Risk: The "Communication & Confidence" Analyst.**

Kunal, your profile shows real delivery: 2+ years at Infosys supporting a multinational semiconductor client, measurable operational impact (20% fewer repeated access requests, 20% faster approval processing, 5+ hours saved weekly on executive reporting), and strong project work (80,000+ transaction analysis at Volt Metrics, 97% phishing-detection accuracy, healthcare cost clustering). Your Resume & Experience Clarity score of 3.2 confirms the material is on the page.

However, your Answer Structure (2.4), Role-Specific Technical (2.4), and Behavioural Story (2.25) reveal a **Communication & Confidence Risk**: in the interview room you risk sounding uncertain, under-structured, and unable to *own* your impact—even when you know the work.

**The Mapping Rule Analysis:**

You can describe tools and tasks (Excel, Power BI, Netskope, SQL, Python), but when probed on *why* a KPI was chosen, *how* you validated a 20% improvement, or *what you personally did* in a cross-functional conflict, answers may trail off, become tool-heavy, or lose STAR structure. Technical Readiness (2.9) shows you have baseline DA knowledge; the gap is not "never learned analytics"—it is **defending your thinking aloud under pressure**.

This "Capable on Paper, Quiet in the Room" persona is your primary hurdle: recruiters in Dublin and Ireland will assume MSc + Infosys = interview-ready, but low confidence and weak storytelling can make you look junior despite solid experience.

sections.title: How This Risk Shows Up in Interviews
sections.content:
**Scenario A: The Resume Walkthrough (10–15m)**

**The Red Flag:** "Kunal, walk me through how you achieved a 20% reduction in repeated access requests at Infosys. What was broken, what did you analyse, and how did you prove the improvement?"

**Justification:** With Answer Structure at 2.4, you are likely to list activities ("I analysed records in Excel", "I used Netskope") instead of a crisp STAR: baseline problem → your analysis method → specific action → validated metric. Interviewers hear process, not ownership.

---

**Scenario B: The Technical / Case Follow-Up (20–30m)**

**The Red Flag:** "You built customer segmentation in Power BI for Volt Metrics—how did you choose four segments? What DAX or SQL logic backed that, and how did you validate it wasn't overfitting noise?"

**Justification:** Role-Specific Technical 2.4 means follow-ups on segmentation logic, DAX measures, and validation may expose shallow depth. You might say "I used Power BI and Python" without explaining feature choice, business thresholds, or how segments changed CRM strategy.

---

**Scenario C: The Behavioural + Stakeholder Probe (10–15m)**

**The Red Flag:** "Tell me about a time you had to push back on a client stakeholder or resolve disagreement using data. What was the conflict and what changed because of *you*?"

**Justification:** Behavioural Story 2.25 is your lowest score. You have cross-functional collaboration material (5–10 member team, 3 executive stakeholders), but without rehearsed structure the *conflict* and *your judgment* disappear—you describe teamwork, not personal impact.

sections.title: Priority Fix Order

steps.title: Confidence + STAR Story Bank
steps.content: Build 5 STAR stories from Infosys (access requests, KPI framework, Netskope policies, executive reports, RCA). Record yourself—each story must finish in 90 seconds with a clear Result metric. **Score Target:** Answer Structure 2.4 → 3.8, Behavioural Story 2.25 → 3.5

steps.title: Metric Defence Drill
steps.content: For every % on your resume (20%, 40%, 97%), write: baseline, measurement method, sample size, timeframe, and one sentence on what would have happened without your change. **Score Target:** Role-Specific Technical 2.4 → 4.0, Resume Clarity 3.2 → 4.2

steps.title: Project Deep-Dives (Volt Metrics + ML)
steps.content: Prepare verbal defences for Volt Metrics segmentation, Phishing pipeline (why RoBERTa + which features), and Healthcare clustering/classification. Practice explaining one SQL query and one DAX measure out loud. **Score Target:** Technical Readiness 2.9 → 4.2

steps.title: The Pressure Test
steps.content: Full mock: Tell Me About Yourself → Infosys walkthrough → technical follow-up on Power BI → behavioural stakeholder conflict → Ireland role motivation. No notes, no apologies, no filler words. **Score Target:** Overall Average → 4.5

sections.content: Complete each phase before moving to the next. Week 1 is non-negotiable—confidence builds from repetition, not reading.

sections.title: Resume-Anchored Technical Prep
sections.content:
**Experience: Infosys — 20% Reduction in Repeated Access Requests**

**Interviewer Probe:** "You analysed 1,000+ operational access records quarterly—what exactly defined a 'repeated' request? How did you establish baseline vs. after? What did you recommend?"

**Likely Struggle:** Mapping to Role-Specific Technical (2.4), you may say "I found patterns in Excel" without defining duplicate criteria, time window, or how the 20% was calculated and signed off by the client.

**Prep Drill:** Write: (1) definition of repeated access, (2) baseline rate over 2–3 quarters, (3) root causes found, (4) policy/process change, (5) post-change measurement. Practice: "I defined repeated requests as the same user–application pair requested more than twice within 30 days. Baseline was X% of 1,000+ records per quarter; after standardising approval rules and risk tagging, repeats dropped 20% over the next two quarters."

---

**Project 1: Volt Metrics — BI & Customer Analytics (40% Less Manual Reporting)**

**Interviewer Probe:** "How did you segment customers into four high-value groups? What variables did you use in SQL/Python, and how did segments inform CRM strategy?"

**Likely Struggle:** You might describe dashboards without explaining segmentation methodology, DAX KPIs, or business rules for "high-value."

**Prep Drill:** List features (RFM, revenue, frequency, product category), clustering or rule-based logic, and one CRM action per segment. Prepare one example DAX measure (e.g., revenue per active customer) and one SQL aggregation across 80,000+ transactions.

---

**Project 2: Phishing Detection — Explainable AI (97% Accuracy)**

**Interviewer Probe:** "Why RoBERTa embeddings plus traditional ML? How did you split train/test? What does 'explainable' mean in your pipeline—what features drove a false positive?"

**Likely Struggle:** Academic projects often sound like "we got 97% accuracy" without train/test split, class imbalance handling, or error analysis—weak under Ireland DA technical screens.

**Prep Drill:** Document: dataset size (11,000+ URLs), features, model choice rationale, validation method, precision/recall trade-off, and one example of explainability (SHAP, feature importance, or error case walkthrough).

---

**Project 3: Healthcare — Drug Spending & Facility Analysis**

**Interviewer Probe:** "How did you define four cost-based drug clusters? Why Logistic Regression vs. Random Forest for facility classification—and how did you evaluate performance?"

**Likely Struggle:** You may stay at "we used ML" without metrics (accuracy, AUC, confusion matrix) or business interpretation for cost-control decisions.

**Prep Drill:** For clustering: algorithm, elbow/silhouette or business thresholds. For classification: metric chosen, cross-validation, and what facility characteristic mattered most for nursing facility outcomes.

sections.title: Interview Answer Construction Guidance
sections.content:
**Experience:** 20% faster manual approval processing via Netskope workflow analysis at Infosys.

**Baseline Answer (Score 2.4 — Communication & Confidence Weakness):**
"At Infosys I worked on Netskope for a semiconductor client. I looked at operational data and found inefficiencies. I helped implement some policies. Approvals became faster by about 20%. I also made Power BI reports and worked with the team."

**Fixed Answer (Score 4.5+ — Structured & Confident):**
"Our semiconductor client was losing time on manual access approvals—average turnaround was roughly [X] days, and analysts were re-submitting similar requests because policies weren't standardised. (Situation) I was asked to reduce approval cycle time without weakening security controls. (Task) I analysed Netskope workflow logs and operational approval data in Excel and SQL, mapped bottlenecks to ten recurring policy gaps, and partnered with security and client ops to implement standardised approval templates and escalation rules. (Action) Over two release cycles, median manual approval time dropped by 20%, we cut repeated access requests by 20% through clearer risk tagging, and executives received weekly KPI packs that saved 5+ hours of manual reporting per week. (Result)"

**Justification:** The fixed version uses STAR, names *your* analysis and collaboration, ties tools to outcomes, and sounds decisive—directly targeting Answer Structure and Behavioural Story gaps.

sections.title: High-Risk Questions (The Landmines)
sections.content:
"How exactly did you measure the 20% reduction in repeated access requests—what was the baseline period and sample?" **(Risk: Role-Specific Technical 2.4)**

"Walk me through one DAX measure you built for operational KPIs at Infosys. What business question did it answer?" **(Risk: Role-Specific Technical 2.4)**

"How did you choose four customer segments in Volt Metrics—what features and what business action followed each segment?" **(Risk: Technical Readiness 2.9)**

"Your phishing model hit 97% accuracy—what was precision on the minority class? Show me how you'd explain a false positive to a non-technical stakeholder." **(Risk: Communication & Confidence)**

"Tell me about a time you disagreed with a stakeholder on data or priorities. What was the conflict and how did you resolve it?" **(Risk: Behavioural Story 2.25)**

"Why are you targeting Data Analyst roles in Ireland after MSc at NCI—and how does your Infosys experience transfer?" **(Risk: Answer Structure 2.4)**

"Describe a root cause analysis you led on operational trends—what was the problem, your hypothesis, and the outcome?" **(Risk: Behavioural Story 2.25)**

sections.title: Mock Interview Plan (Mentor-Led)

data.label: Session 1: Tell Me About Yourself + Infosys Walkthrough
data.objective: Build opening confidence and STAR flow on Infosys impact metrics. Raise Answer Structure.

data.label: Session 2: DA Technical Deep-Dive
data.objective: Power BI/DAX, SQL, KPI design, Volt Metrics segmentation. Push on validation and methodology.

data.label: Session 3: Behavioural + Stakeholder Impact
data.objective: Executive reporting, cross-functional RCA, conflict stories. Target Behavioural Story 2.25 → 4.0.

data.label: Session 4: Full Ireland DA Simulation
data.objective: Resume + technical + behavioural + motivation under time pressure. Gate before applications.

sections.content:
**Session 1: Tell Me About Yourself + Infosys Walkthrough**

**Focus:** 90-second intro (MSc NCI + Infosys DA + target Ireland roles) and two STAR stories with metrics.

**Mentor Push:** Stop filler ("basically", "kind of", "I think"). Interrupt if Kunal lists tools without impact. Require eye contact and steady pace—no rushing endings.

---

**Session 2: DA Technical Deep-Dive**

**Focus:** KPI framework (5–10 KPIs), Netskope workflow analysis, Volt Metrics SQL/Python + Power BI.

**Mentor Push:** Ask "How did you validate?" after every percentage. If answer is vague, assign homework: one-page metric defence before Session 3.

---

**Session 3: Behavioural + Stakeholder Impact**

**Focus:** Executive reports for 3 stakeholders, cross-functional RCA, personal conflict/ownership.

**Mentor Push:** Reject team-only answers. Demand: "What did *you* recommend? Who pushed back? What changed?"

---

**Session 4: Full Ireland DA Simulation**

**Focus:** Realistic Dublin hiring loop—mix of resume, SQL/Power BI, ML project summary, and behavioural.

**Mentor Push:** Simulate nervousness triggers (silence, follow-up "why"). Pass only if average mock score ≥ 4.5/5.

sections.title: Expected Outcome
sections.content:
**Target Average Score: 4.5**

**Measurable Change:**

- Move from "I analysed data in Excel and Power BI" to "I defined repeated access as [criteria], measured a 20% reduction over [timeframe], and implemented [specific policy changes] validated with client sign-off."
- Move from "97% accuracy on phishing" to "RoBERTa + ML pipeline on 11,000+ URLs with [split/validation], precision/recall trade-off, and explainable drivers for false positives."
- The "After" Persona: A **confident Ireland-ready Data Analyst** who narrates impact clearly, defends metrics under pressure, and owns stakeholder stories—not someone who hides behind tools or team wording.

sections.title: How to Use This Plan

candidateSteps.title: Complete Week 1 STAR bank before Session 1
candidateSteps.content: Five stories recorded on video (90 sec each). No Session 1 until you can deliver Infosys 20% metrics without notes.

candidateSteps.title: One-page metric defence per resume claim
candidateSteps.content: After each session, document questions where you hesitated or apologised. Fix within 24 hours—confidence gaps compound if delayed.

candidateSteps.title: Daily 10-minute out-loud drill
candidateSteps.content: Read one fixed answer (like the Netskope example) aloud daily. Ireland interviews reward clear spoken English and pace—not only correct content.

candidateSteps.title: Do NOT apply until Session 4 ≥ 4.5/5
candidateSteps.content: Low Behavioural (2.25) + Structure (2.4) will fail screening even with strong projects. Use mocks as gates, not encouragement.

mentorSteps.title: Coach confidence, not just content
mentorSteps.content: If Kunal trails off, stop and restart the same question. Do not accept mumbled endings—require a clear Result sentence every time.

mentorSteps.title: Probe every metric until validated or admitted
mentorSteps.content: Push on baselines for 20%, 40%, 97%. Document knowledge boundaries honestly—pretending hurts Ireland offers.

mentorSteps.title: Written feedback: structure + delivery
mentorSteps.content: Score both content and delivery (pace, filler words, ownership language). Track weekly movement on Structure and Behavioural.

mentorSteps.title: Reset expectations
mentorSteps.content: Passing Session 4 means interview-competitive, not guaranteed offers. Dublin market also tests visa/right-to-work and domain fit—keep mocks realistic.

sections.content:
**Non-negotiable rule:**
If Session 4 score is <4.5/5, repeat Sessions 2–4 in Week 5. Do not mass-apply to Ireland DA roles until behavioural and structure scores improve.

**Timeline:**
- Week 1: STAR story bank + video self-review
- Week 2: Sessions 1–2 (Walkthrough + DA technical)
- Week 3: Session 3 (Behavioural + stakeholders)
- Week 4: Session 4 (Full simulation)
- Week 5: Buffer for repetition if needed

Start Week 1 today. Email your mentor when all five STAR recordings are done.
